# Coursebook

Welcome to the systems programming coursebook! This repository houses a high-quality, open-source introductory systems programming textbook used by the [CS 341: System Programming](http://cs341.cs.illinois.edu/) course at the [University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign](https://illinois.edu/) The book assumes that you have taken a programming language course and are familiar with assembly instructions. All of the code and instruction will be in C, as it is the de-facto language of the Linux Kernel. The Coursebook is an aim to standardize and build upon Angrave's [original wikibook experiment](https://github.com/angrave/SystemProgramming/wiki). The most recent version of the coursebook as a single pdf is here: [main.pdf](https://github.com/cs341-illinois/coursebook/blob/pdf_deploy/main.pdf). ## Overview ### Goals * Improve the quality and rigour of the original wikibook while maintaining openness. * Improve the factualness by including citations, footnotes, extended reading, and a glossary. * Have exports in the form of pdf, markdown, and html. * Automagically build so writers can focus on writing. ## Contributing, Building, and Structure Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` ## Credit Where Credit is Due * Title Page Idea Inspiration - https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/85904/showcase-of-beautiful-title-page-done-in-tex * Duck Image Inspiration - https://pixabay.com/photos/toy-bath-rubber-duck-studio-1474138/ * Chapter Style Inspiration - https://texblog.org/2012/07/03/fancy-latex-chapter-styles/ * PDF Image Inspiration - https://pixabay.com/illustrations/pdf-miniature-file-icon-2127829/

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, C-based introductory systems programming textbook for the University of Illinois.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository hosts a high-quality, open-source coursebook used for CS 341: System Programming at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. It serves as a comprehensive textbook covering core systems concepts, assuming prior knowledge of basic programming and assembly. All code examples and instruction are written in C, utilizing the POSIX standard since it is the de-facto language of the Linux kernel. The project is maintained as a collaborative wikibook, allowing for continuous updates and improvements from educators and students alike. It provides a deep dive into operating system fundamentals and low-level software design.
keyFeatures: Comprehensive curriculum: Covers core introductory systems programming concepts taught at a university level.
C and POSIX focus: Centers all instruction and code examples around C and the POSIX API.
Open-source wikibook: Allows for community contributions, corrections, and continuous educational improvement.
LaTeX formatting: Utilizes LaTeX for professional, high-quality typesetting of the textbook material.
Practical examples: Includes actionable code snippets that demonstrate low-level Linux interactions.
